subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which property is typical of most metals?
questions.explain: Metals contain delocalised electrons that are free to move, allowing them to conduct electricity well.

questions.q: Aluminium is used for overhead electricity cables mainly because it is:
options: Low in density and a good electrical conductor
A poor conductor with a high density
questions.explain: Its low density keeps the cables light while its good conductivity allows electricity to flow efficiently.

questions.q: Why is copper suitable for electrical wiring?
options: It is a good conductor of electricity and can be drawn into wires
It has a very low melting point
It is the most reactive of all metals
questions.explain: Copper is both an excellent electrical conductor and ductile, so it can be pulled into long wires.

questions.q: Brass is an alloy of which two metals?
questions.explain: Brass is made by mixing copper with zinc.

questions.q: Stainless steel is made from iron mixed mainly with which element?
questions.explain: Stainless steel contains iron alloyed with chromium (and nickel), which resists corrosion.

questions.q: Why is an alloy usually harder than the pure metal it is based on?
options: The different-sized atoms distort the layers so they cannot slide easily
All the atoms are exactly the same size
Alloys are pure substances with perfect layers
Alloys have much weaker metallic bonds
questions.explain: Atoms of different sizes disrupt the regular layers, making it harder for them to slide over each other.

questions.q: Which of these metals is the most reactive?
questions.explain: Potassium sits near the top of the reactivity series, well above iron, copper and gold.

questions.q: A student adds four metals separately to dilute hydrochloric acid. Which one produces no bubbles of gas?
questions.explain: Copper lies below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it does not react with dilute acids to give hydrogen.

questions.q: Which metal will displace copper from copper(II) sulfate solution?
questions.explain: Zinc is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from the solution.

questions.q: Metal X displaces lead from lead(II) nitrate solution but cannot displace iron from iron(II) sulfate solution. Where does X lie in the reactivity series?
questions.explain: X is more reactive than lead but less reactive than iron, so it lies between them.

questions.q: What are the products when potassium reacts with cold water?
questions.explain: Reactive metals react with water to form the metal hydroxide and hydrogen gas.

questions.q: Which two substances are both needed for iron to rust?
questions.explain: Rusting of iron requires both oxygen and water to be present.

questions.q: Rust is chemically best described as:
questions.explain: Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide, formed when iron reacts with oxygen and water.

questions.q: Galvanising protects iron from rusting because the zinc coating:
options: Is more reactive than iron and corrodes in preference to it
Is less reactive than iron and never corrodes
Is a non-metal that repels water
questions.explain: Zinc is more reactive, so it corrodes sacrificially and also forms a barrier over the iron.

questions.q: Blocks of metal are bolted to a steel ship's hull to give sacrificial protection. Which metal is suitable?
questions.explain: Magnesium is more reactive than iron, so it corrodes instead of the steel hull.

questions.q: Aluminium is extracted from its ore by which method?
options: Reduction with carbon in a blast furnace
questions.explain: Aluminium is too reactive to be reduced by carbon, so it is obtained by electrolysis of molten aluminium oxide.

questions.q: Why can aluminium not be extracted by heating its oxide with carbon?
options: Aluminium is more reactive than carbon
Aluminium is less reactive than carbon
questions.explain: Only metals below carbon in the reactivity series can be reduced by carbon; aluminium is above it.

questions.q: In the blast furnace, iron(III) oxide is reduced to iron mainly by:
questions.explain: Carbon monoxide acts as the reducing agent, removing oxygen from the iron(III) oxide.

questions.q: A newly discovered metal lies just below carbon in the reactivity series. Which extraction method is most suitable and cheapest?
options: Leaving it as the native metal only
questions.explain: Metals below carbon in reactivity can be reduced by carbon, which is cheaper than electrolysis.

questions.q: In the extraction of aluminium, cryolite is added to the aluminium oxide in order to:
options: Lower the melting point of the aluminium oxide
Increase the melting point of the aluminium oxide
React with and remove the aluminium
questions.explain: Cryolite lowers the melting point so less energy is needed to keep the mixture molten.
